name: Krampus
description: The horned, chain-rattling demon who deals with the naughty while St Nicholas rewards the good
origin: Alpine folklore of Austria, Bavaria and their neighbours

debut.title: Alpine folk tradition
debut.era: centuries-old customs, on greeting cards from the 1800s

legend: In the Alps, St Nicholas doesn't travel alone. On the night of 5 December, Krampusnacht, the eve of St Nicholas Day, he's joined by Krampus: shaggy, horned and long-tongued, rattling chains and bells. While the saint hands out treats, Krampus swats the naughty with bundles of birch and, in the scarier tellings, stuffs them in a sack or basket and carries them off. In the 1800s Austrians sent each other Krampus greeting cards, and today towns hold Krampuslauf runs where costumed Krampuses charge through the streets.

myths.explanation: His night is 5 December, Krampusnacht, the eve of St Nicholas Day.
They work as a team: the saint rewards the good while Krampus deals with the naughty.

myths.claim: People sent each other Krampus Christmas cards.
myths.explanation: Krampuskarten were popular in Austria from the 1800s, often with the greeting Gruß vom Krampus.

myths.claim: Krampus parades are a thing of the past.
myths.explanation: Krampuslauf runs take place every December across the Alps and increasingly around the world.

powers: A sack big enough for a child
legacy: Krampuskarten, the Austrian greeting cards of the 1800s and early 1900s
Krampuslauf runs in towns from Salzburg to Los Angeles
Krampus (2015), a horror comedy directed by Michael Dougherty
facts: Krampus is a horned, hairy creature from Alpine folklore
He accompanies St Nicholas, who rewards the good while Krampus punishes the naughty
His night is 5 December, Krampusnacht, the eve of St Nicholas Day
He carries chains, bells and bundles of birch switches called Ruten
Naughty children might be stuffed into his sack or basket and carried away
In Krampuslauf parades, costumed Krampuses charge through town streets
Austrians sent each other Krampus greeting cards in the 1800s
hostIntro: First guest of the season, and he's brought his own chains. He's on a list of his own, and he's checking yours twice.
